checklist.item: A sub-sill with end dams and a back leg is shown under the storefront, weeped to the exterior.
checklist.why: Storefront is drained glazing: water gets in and must be led out at the sill.

checklist.item: Sub-sill end dams are sealed and the sill is set in sealant with shims that do not block the weeps.
checklist.why: Missing end dams send the water into the jambs.

checklist.item: The wall's water barrier laps onto the sub-sill or its flashing, and the air barrier is sealed to the frame.
checklist.why: The frame must be tied to the wall's barriers.

checklist.item: Door threshold height and bevel meet the accessibility limit, and the landing slopes away without exceeding the allowed slope.
Frame thermal break lines up with the wall insulation and the slab edge is insulated.
checklist.why: A sill on bare slab edge condenses.

checklist.item: Glazing type (safety glazing near doors and floors), anchors and sealant joints are noted.
